restricted_paired_comparison_excluding_p.note: subset = TEST episodes where the proposed policy did NOT abstain/escalate; fixed-priority-sequential is scored on the identical subset for a fair paired comparison (it never abstains, so it has a defined outcome on every episode)

honest_reframing: On the raw (abstention-inclusive) metric the frozen result shows proposed (0.7029) losing to fixed-priority-sequential (0.7514), a statistically significant regression. But the proposed policy abstained on 11.0% of episodes, and every abstention scores as a non-success by construction. Restricted to the 623 episodes where it chose to act, proposed succeeds 0.7897 of the time vs. fixed-priority's 0.7865 on that identical subset (McNemar p=0.883). This does not overturn the frozen H4 verdict -- the pre-registered metric is what it is, and the verdict against it stands -- but it shows the negative headline effect is substantially attributable to how abstention is scored, not to the proposed policy's action-selection being worse than the fixed rule when it does act.
